item.title: Top stories in Azerbaijan, Armenia, and Georgia from 1-5 December, 2025
item.description: Daily morning roundup. Top stories in local media, commentary, trending photos and videos.

item.title: Hundreds of children study in shelters every day: how Ukraine’s underground schools work
item.description: These schools now operate in eastern, northern, and southern regions, where studying in the usual format is unsafe.

item.title: ‘Ensuring safety at every inch’: demining effort in Armenia
item.description: Mine detection and disposal is carried out more actively in the border regions. This does not mean that other areas are completely cleared.

item.title: Another archbishop arrested in Armenia over drug-related charges
item.description: Archbishop Arshak Khachatryan is accused of ordering drugs to be planted in the backpack of a protester opposing the Catholicos. Earlier, two other archbishops were arrested in politically motivated cases.

item.title: Kremlin overseer: “There are no anti-Russian sentiments in Abkhazia”
item.description: Sergey Kirienko commented on the sensitive issues in Russian-Abkhazian relations

item.title: Amnesty International: probe “kamit” use in Georgia, impose police equipment embargo on the country
item.description: The organization criticizes the “hostile activity” charges brought against experts, witnesses, and human rights defenders who acted as BBC respondents

item.title: “This is not ‘кamit’” – Georgian security services officially refute BBC claims of chemical poisoning of protesters
item.description: SSG: “Chlorobenzylidene malononitrile, which is not a banned substance, was added to the water cannons. All BBC respondents deny saying anything about the use of the poisonous substance ‘kamit'"

item.title: “The regime is poisoning us!” — thousands march in Tbilisi demanding an international investigation. Photos&video
item.description: March against the alleged use of the World War I-era chemical “kamit” on protesters. Participants said the security service’s comments only reinforced their suspicions

item.title: “Tbilisi is testing Baku’s patience” – pro-government Azerbaijani media sharply criticize Georgia
item.description: Minval: "Baku is ready to supply Armenia with Azerbaijani oil products. The only route is through Georgia — but Tbilisi has inflated the transit price 40-fold"
